texts.preamble: Alpeshbhai Babubhai Pathodiya vs State Of Gujarat on 4 December, 2018 Author: Mohinder Pal Bench: Mohinder Pal, A.C. Rao C/Fa/3913/2017 Order
texts.facts: By way of this petition, petitioner has challenged the order dated 24.9,2015 passed by Adjudicating Officer and Resident Additional Collector, Surendranagar in Adjudicating Application No.NFSA/FSSA-06-Case No.6/2015 as well as order dated 28.03.2017 passed by the learned Presiding Officer, Food Safety Appellate Tribunal, State of Gujarat, Gandhinagar in Appeal No.28 of 2015, wherein, petitioner has been imposed penalty of Rs.2 Lacs. 2. Facts giving rise to this petition are that on 27.08.2013, at around 9.30 a.m. one Mr.Parmar, District Purvatha Officer along with other official had visited the premises of the petitioner. Sample of edible oil was taken, which was sent for analysis and was found to be substandard. Challan was presented before the concerned Authority and ultimately petitioner has been imposed penalty of Alpeshbhai Babubhai Pathodiya vs State Of Gujarat on 4 December, 2018 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/152043780/ 1 Rs.2 Lacs. Petitioner preferred appeal which also came to be dismissed. Aggrieved from this decision, petitioner has approached this Court.
texts.arguments: 3. Learned counsel for the petitioner has submitted that the Court below has not taken into consideration general provisions while imposing penalty. It has been submitted that as per Section 49 of the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006, the concerned official was required to take into consideration various aspects including profit earned by the petitioner, loss caused to the human body on account of excess material found in the samples and nature of contravention and intention of the seller. It has been submitted that all the aforementioned facts are not taken into consideration.
texts.petitioner_arguments: 3. Learned counsel for the petitioner has submitted that the Court below has not taken into consideration general provisions while imposing penalty. It has been submitted that as per Section 49 of the Food Safety and Standards Act, 2006, the concerned official was required to take into consideration various aspects including profit earned by the petitioner, loss caused to the human body on account of excess material found in the samples and nature of contravention and intention of the seller. It has been submitted that all the aforementioned facts are not taken into consideration.
